Incumbent Republican U.S. Senator [[Arlen Specter]] won re-election to a fourth term. Primary elections were held on May 19, 1998. In the Republican primary, Specter defeated minor challengers from his right. Lloyd won the Democratic primary with a plurality of the vote over Richard J. Cusick and Richard J. Lloyd Jr.]], state representative from [[Somerset, Pennsylvania|Somerset]]{{cite news|title=Demo Lawmaker Wants Specter's Job|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/392840766|access-date=August 20, 2010|newspaper=Allentown Morning Call|date=January 6, 1998}} (Democratic) *Dean Snyder (Constitution) * [[Arlen Specter]], incumbent U.S. senator since 1981 (Republican) ===Campaign=== Leading up to this campaign, the state Democratic Party faced difficulty, as it was plagued by prior corruption allegations of several key legislators and by a lack of fund-raising. Just as in the accompanying [[Pennsylvania gubernatorial election, 1998|gubernatorial race]], the party had difficulty in finding a credible candidate. State Representative Bill Lloyd, who was a well-respected party leader but who had little statewide name recognition, was considered by Democratic party leaders{{cite news |last1=Leffler |first1=Pete |title=DEMOCRAT BILL LLOYD'S DRIVING FOR SPECTER'S SENATE SEAT LITERALLY. THE STATE REPRESENTATIVE IS MOTORING AROUND PA., AND BLAMES LACK OF MONEY FOR HIS LOW CAMPAIGN PROFILE. |url=https://www.mcall.com/news/mc-xpm-1998-09-29-3206214-story.html |access-date=18 March 2021 |publisher=The Morning Call |date=29 September 1998}} to be a sacrificial lamb candidate. Specter ran a straightforward campaign and attempted to avoid mistakes, while Lloyd's bid was so underfunded that he was unable to air a single commercial until two weeks before the election. Lloyd's strategy was to portray Republicans as hyper-partisan in wake of their attempt to impeach President [[Bill Clinton]], but he was unable to gain any traction with his message. On Election Day, Specter's win was by the second-largest margin in the history of Senate elections in Pennsylvania. Lloyd won only two counties: almost uniformly Democratic [[Philadelphia]] and his home county, rural and typically Republican [[Somerset County, Pennsylvania|Somerset County]].{{cite book|last=Kennedy|first=John J.|title=Pennsylvania Elections: Statewide Contests from 1950-2004|date=2006|publisher=United Press of America|isbn=9780761832799|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1J_9q-lIWRkC&q=1998+specter+lloyd&pg=PA75}} As of 2022, this is the last time [[Allegheny County, Pennsylvania|Allegheny County]] voted for a Republican Senate candidate. ===Polling=== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign=bottom !
